notes.summary: New arbitrary-dimensional finite-PA contact criterion: noncontact forces a zero-cost positive tangent relation; any growth-compatible PA function with that relation and positive raw mass yields an explicit admissible obstacle with exact envelope and negative contact. General regularizable endpoints remain unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: On finite pure positive balanced rational embedded X, use the printed rational-endpoint PC class and separate PA_Z/PA_R coefficients. At a PA germ, generator slopes s are PC exactly when s·lambda>=0 for K={lambda>=0:Ulambda=0}. If a finite PA envelope is noncontact at a vertex, some nonzero lambda has cost zero. Conversely, for f in PAPC_* with bounded PA difference from the actual reference gamma, a flat relation and positive primitive-normal raw atom m_v give u=f-gamma+(R-rho(x-v))_+, with rational R and lattice norm rho, P_gamma(u)=f, and integral=-R m_v. Every measured endpoint is already PA and regularizable. This gives necessary and sufficient conditions only for the finite PA endpoint sector.
notes.text:
Let X subset N_R be finite, pure of positive dimension d, rational, and carry strictly positive balanced top weights. PA_Z means integral tangent slopes/rational constants; PA_R means real affine coefficients on a finite rational structure. Competitors remain all printed-PC functions, subject to the actual growth upper bound. At a vertex v of a carrying structure for PA PC f, write its linear tangent germ h. Choose nonzero rational generators d_i of all tangent cones, including opposite generators for lineality, and set U=(d_i), s_i=h(d_i), K={lambda>=0:Ulambda=0}. A flat relation is nonzero lambda in K with s·lambda=0.

The local support equivalence is proved as follows. Scaled generator endpoints give genuine PCCs, so PC implies s·lambda>=0. The finitely generated closed cone T=R_+^m+image(U^T) has dual K. Closure follows by eliminating dependent positive representations to independent subsets, whose coefficient inverses have bounded norm. If s is outside T, nearest-point separation gives a nonnegative lambda with Ulambda=0 and s·lambda<0. Thus s=U^T ell+b, b>=0, yielding an ambient affine local support. Conversely local supports imply convexity on every segment: after subtracting an endpoint chord, a positive maximum has both an open and closed maximum set, since its supporting slope must vanish. A support at a PCC center then gives f(x_i)>=f(x)+ell(x_i-x); summation proves all PCCs on every structure. This reconstructs the support argument on the general domain, rather than applying A224's fan theorem outside its scope. At other faces the same generator test includes tangent lineality; it is finite and rational.

There is no flat relation iff there is a strictly lower affine floor: h(x)-ell(x)>=c||x|| for all tangent-support x, some c>0. Positive spanning from B225 applies to each inherited positive balanced star. The normalized section of K is compact and nonempty; when all costs are positive its minimum theta>0. Apply the preceding separation to s-delta*1, 0<delta<theta, then compactness of the unit cone sections gives c. If the actual envelope f is noncontact at v, continuity of the obstacle gives a neighborhood with gap eta>0. Raise f locally to max(f,f(v)+t+ell(x-v)), with t smaller than eta and the collar margin. It equals f near the neighborhood boundary, lies below the obstacle, preserves growth, and has local supports everywhere. It is an unrestricted PC competitor raising f(v), a contradiction. The floor can have irrational breaks and receives no operator. Hence noncontact of a PA envelope forces a flat relation.

Conversely suppose f belongs to PAPC_* and f-gamma is bounded PA in the same category, and a flat relation occurs at a vertex with genuine raw atom m_v>0. Choose an integral-coordinate norm rho=max|x_j| and rational R>0 with its closed ball wholly in the affine star of f and containing no other carrying vertex. Put B=(R-rho(x-v))_+ and u=f-gamma+B. This obstacle is bounded PA; B is literal PA, so both coefficient categories are respected. For a flat relation choose rational roof-boundary endpoints y_i=v+R d_i/rho(d_i) and coefficients beta_i=lambda_i rho(d_i)/R. Their normalized barycenter is v and their average f-value equals f(v). Since B(y_i)=0, any competitor q has q(v)<=f(v). Every rational x in the roof interior lies on a segment from v to the rational boundary point in its incident cell, where f is affine. Jensen gives q(x)<=f(x). Outside the roof q<=f directly. Small rational simplices and continuity of f extend the bound to all real points, without assuming q continuous. Thus P_gamma(u)=f over every printed-PC competitor. The endpoint is PA and has a constant decreasing regularization. Only v contributes to the gap, so its exact integral is -R m_v.

The raw formula is D_f c(tau)=sum c_sigma f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)-f_tau(sum c_sigma n_sigma/tau), with primitive saturated inward normals, and MA_*(f)=D_f^d[X]. No extra factorial is inserted. Genuine balancing/refinement are checked through the complete BBGS publisher2022 proof units Proposition 3.12, Proposition 3.15, Lemma 3.18, Proposition 3.19, printed pages1639-1643, including their full dependency chain. With tangent-lattice covolumes a, projection(n)=(a_sigma/a_tau)nu and BBGS's negative-sign product with -f of weights a_sigma c_sigma equals a_tau D_f c. Saturation proves the height formula, and balancing cancels tangent extensions. Repeat at every stage; a_vertex=1. Local supports give positivity against every intermediate nonnegative balanced cycle. This is the literal raw operator and its explicit real-linear finite-PA extension, never an operator on every continuous completion.

Consequently all admissible obstacles whose envelopes are themselves PAPC_* have zero raw contact iff every relative PAPC_* f satisfies m_v>0 => no flat relation at every vertex. Necessity is the constructed roof; sufficiency is the preceding noncontact theorem at each of finitely many atoms. This is a new scoped theorem, not closure of original P05.2: PA regularization of arbitrary envelopes and contact for non-PA regularizable limits remain unproved. R230 is used only within its completion/envelope scope; it is not reproved.

notes.summary: Finite algebraic obstruction test on each specified rational carrying structure: shared-face PC constraints and actual recession-growth equalities, one zero extreme relation cost, and positive raw mass polynomial. No uniform bound on carrying refinements or general approximation theorem is proved.
notes.detailedSummary: PA affine coefficients z satisfy finite rational continuity equations and local PC inequalities. Bounded difference from gamma is exactly equality of recession slopes on all cells. The primitive-normal recursion gives m_v(z) a degree-d polynomial. The bad real-PA sector carried by that structure is exactly a finite semialgebraic disjunction with one zero extreme relation cost and m_v>0. Literal candidates additionally require integral tangent linear parts and rational constants; real feasibility cannot be promoted to literal feasibility.
notes.text:
Fix a finite rational carrying structure Pi for the actual reference gamma and the balanced cycle. Parameterize cell affine coefficients of f by z. Equality on shared faces is checked on rational affine bases. By n1, PC is exactly a finite set Az>=0: at each face enumerate extreme rays of K={lambda>=0:Ulambda=0} and test the generator-slope costs. Extreme rays have one-dimensional kernels on minimally dependent positive supports of size at most rank(U)+1; rational Gaussian elimination gives their normalized rational coefficients. Thus non-simplicial stars need no replacement by ambient strong convexity.

For every recession generator r of every cell sigma impose (f_sigma-gamma_sigma)(r)=0. Necessity follows by restriction to x+tr. Sufficiency follows from a cell's finite vertex-plus-recession representation, or after cutting by rational coordinate hyperplanes into pointed cells. R230's elementary rational cone-section argument applied to the homogenized cell proves this representation; lineality uses both signs. These equations encode the whole actual bounded-difference growth condition, not degree or a reference surrogate.

Raw m_v(z) is a homogeneous degree-d polynomial in linear parts by the genuine recursion in n1, with coefficients determined by actual weights and saturated primitive normals. On a specified structure the existence of a bad growth-compatible real-PA f is exactly the finite disjunction: shared-face equations, Az>=0, recession equalities, s_v(z)·kappa_vj=0 for an extreme relation, and m_v(z)>0. Every extreme cost is nonnegative, so a zero-cost nonnegative relation exists iff some extreme cost is zero. Each feasible point supplies n1's exact roof obstacle and measured PA endpoint. In PA_Z impose integral tangent coordinates in saturated lattice bases and rational constants as additional arithmetic restrictions. Real solutions do not supply literal ones.

A true common lineality on which the germ is affine forces flat opposite-generator relations, but the raw top atom is zero: every face of the corresponding generalized carrying fan contains that lineality, leaving no zero-dimensional faces. Refinement independence preserves zero after artificial cuts.

This is an algebraic test for a supplied structure, not a finite classification of all structures and not a regularity theorem. There is no proved uniform bound on refinements needed by an unrestricted envelope. Artifacts: P05.2-paper.tex sections3-6, argument.md, source-application-ledger.md, check_certificates.py. Rerun: python check_certificates.py; pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error P05.2-paper.tex twice. The exact checker enumerates the stated finite positive circuits and verifies a symbolic mass polynomial; those computations are finite evidence, not continuum proof.

notes.summary: Fully realized nonseparable two-dimensional contact obstruction on two coordinate planes meeting along a line: exact PA envelope has raw masses8,4,4 and total16, equal to the reference mass, but contact integral -2.
notes.detailedSummary: X={y=0} union {x=0} in Z^3_R, eight top quadrants weight1. Gamma=|x|+|y|+|z| is literal PA PC and positive at infinity. f=max(|x|,|y|-1,0)+|z| has bounded literal PA difference from gamma and a flat opposing-y relation. For u=f-gamma+(1/4-max(|x|,|y|,|z|))_+, n1 proves P_gamma(u)=f over all competitors. Primitive raw masses are8 at0 and4 at each(0,+/-1,0); the integral is -2. This is a valid endpoint obstruction, not pair-level regularity for other obstacles.
notes.text:
Take N=Z^3, X={y=0} union {x=0}, each of the eight coordinate quadrants with weight1. Each tangent plane is saturated and unimodular. On an x/y axis, inward transverse normals are +/-e_z; on the shared z axis they are +/-e_x,+/-e_y. Their sums vanish, proving positive balancing. Gamma=|x|+|y|+|z| restricts an ambient convex norm and is positive in every nonzero recession direction. Define f=max(|x|,|y|-1,0)+|z| on X. It too restricts an ambient convex function. It is literal PA with rational breaks y=+/-1 and z=0; f-gamma is0 on the horizontal plane and -min(|y|,1) on the vertical plane, so is bounded literal PA.

Near0 the six slopes (x+,x-,y+,y-,z+,z-) are(1,1,0,0,1,1). The positive relation cone has exactly the three opposing pairs. Writing A=s_x++s_x-, B=s_y++s_y-, C=s_z++s_z-, PC is A,B,C>=0 and the first raw weights on x+/-,y+/-,z+/- are respectively C,C,A+B. The second atom polynomial is 2C(A+B). At f: A=2,B=0,C=2, giving atom8 and a zero-cost y pair. The complete first cycle has weight2 along all three axes and weight1 along each line(0,+/-1,z). At p=(0,+/-1,0), outgoing y slopes are0 toward0 and1 away; z slopes are1,1. Primitive weights2,2,1,1 give mass4. These cycles balance, with no other atoms. Thus MA(f)=8delta0+4delta(0,1,0)+4delta(0,-1,0). Gamma has sole raw atom16. No factorial is added to these recursive computations.

For R=1/4 and rho=max(|x|,|y|,|z|), u=f-gamma+(R-rho)_+ is bounded continuous literal PA and nonseparable. It is n1's exact roof: P_gamma(u)=f. The measured endpoint itself is literal PA and regularizable, independently of the unknown domain of other envelopes. The roof includes only the origin among its raw atoms. Therefore the exact contact integral is -R*8=-2, despite equal total mass16. This formula does not reuse or repair failed product ansatz229.

Exact standard-library evidence in certificate-input.json, check_certificates.py and evidence/certificate-output.json: three positive circuit rays, eight saturated top quadrants, six primitive-normal balances, symbolic polynomial2C(A+B),729 slope vectors exhausted on {0,1,2}^6,561 distinct grid points,448 radial chord cases,3 scaled flat PCCs, and85 rational-kink monotonicity cases all passed. Two oblique saturated-plane covolume checks also passed: facet squared covolumes1 and6, plane squared covolume5, and projected primitive height squares5 and5/6. These finite results do not certify continuum maximality; n1 and the direct raw calculation prove it. Rerun: python check_certificates.py. Paper and full proof: P05.2-paper.tex/P05.2-paper.pdf and argument.md. This example does not classify arbitrary pairs or establish pair-level real regularity.

notes.summary: PA_R on finite rational structures is not closed under maxima, even for convex functions with common reference growth. The displayed irrational-kink maximum is nevertheless literally regularizable, so this is no endpoint nonregularizability counterexample.
notes.detailedSummary: On R take alpha=sqrt2-1, f1=|x| and f2=|x-1|+alpha. Both are PA_R on rational structures and have bounded difference from |x|, while their maximum is |x-t|+t at irrational t=sqrt2/2, outside PA_R. Rational t_n decreasing to t give literal PA PC H_n=max(x,2t_n-x), uniformly decreasing to the maximum with exact error2(t_n-t). Hence a finite maximum or hull argument requires its own carrying-structure audit and cannot infer regularization failure from the irrational break.
notes.text:
Let alpha=sqrt2-1 and t=(1+alpha)/2=sqrt2/2. f1=|x| and f2=|x-1|+alpha are continuous convex real-PA functions with rational breakpoints0 and1. Both differ boundedly from gamma=|x|. For x<=0, f2 dominates; for x>=1, f1 dominates; in [0,1], f1=x and f2=1+alpha-x=2t-x. Thus H=max(f1,f2)=max(x,2t-x)=|x-t|+t globally. Its unique kink is irrational. A finite rational polyhedral structure on the line can only have rational vertices, so it cannot carry H.

Choose rational t_n decreasing to t. H_n=max(x,2t_n-x) has integral slopes +/-1 and rational constant2t_n on a rational carrying structure, is PC and has bounded difference from gamma. It decreases pointwise to H, and sup_R|H_n-H|=2(t_n-t). Thus H is in the literal regularizable domain despite not being PA_R; no MA assignment is made here. In particular absence of closure under max is not evidence that a continuous-obstacle envelope fails regularization.

The finite evidence uses certified square comparisons to bound t at denominators10,100,...,1000000 and85 pointwise monotonicity cases. Upper brackets are4/5,71/100,177/250,442/625,70711/100000,707107/1000000. Their uniform error upper bounds are1/5,1/50,1/500,1/5000,1/50000,1/500000. These finite brackets corroborate, but do not replace, the exact algebraic proof. Artifacts: check_certificates.py, evidence/certificate-output.json, P05.2-paper.tex section8. Rerun: python check_certificates.py.

notes.summary: Deliverable completed as a scoped research draft, not the entire original classification. Paper/PDF, full argument, retained task/grants, source audit, programs and evidence exist. General real regularization, non-PA contact and exhaustive global geometric classification remain open; candidate=false.
notes.detailedSummary: The new theorem covers arbitrary-dimensional finite PA endpoints and actual growth-compatible obstruction functions, with an exact algebraic test on each fixed structure. It does not show all admissible envelopes lie in a regularizable operator domain, extend the certificate criterion to non-PA limits, bound relevant carrying refinements, or characterize all globally realizable singular jets. A224's accepted obstruction, B225's compact/positive-spanning results and R230's completion remain in their proved scopes. Local build/check success is reproducibility evidence only.
notes.text:
The unchanged original asks for every admissible obstacle and every genuine regularizable-envelope/operator antecedent, in separate literal and explicit real-scalar categories. The present results do not close that request. In particular n1's exact equivalence covers PA endpoints only; n2 is a finite algebraic test on a specified structure, with no bound over all refinements. We have neither general real-PA approximation of the continuous envelopes supplied by R230, nor an operator on those merely continuous endpoints, nor contact for every regularizable non-PA limit. We have not solved the global extension problem for every local bad jet with the actual reference. These omissions prevent a necessary-and-sufficient structural classification of all pairs. A224's accepted strict-active-coefficient U(3,4) obstruction remains context, not a pair-level real regularity theorem; the literal source zero-coefficient strictness issue is disclosed. No supplied-book assertion or failed product observation is a grant.
